## Explicit model defect claims (subject to independent verification)

### Does a node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, whose newest configuration entry is inside the persisted commit index and has no covering snapshot, still know that configuration after NewRaft returns?

Current disposition: active.
Question `9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-question-0` v1; sources: newraft_scan, restore_committed, newraft_doc, cfg_doc, snapshot_config, process_config_entry, follower_abort ([full references](state.json)).
Current model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification).

Current interpretation `4099b8f3cc5c45d2b3c3049ce5a5c0de-interpretation-0` · declared predicate does not hold: Summary of the current account for this question: the trigger is RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore, a log whose newest configuration entry is at or below the persisted commit index, and no snapshot whose ConfigurationIndex covers that entry. Under that trigger the restarted node reconstructs its configuration only from the snapshot, so three consequence classes follow, each with retained control-backed receipts, plus a client-contract consequence recorded further below: (a) a missing membership context - empty configuration when there is no snapshot, which stops all campaigns and leaves a live quorum unable to elect (receipts 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc, 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a, 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837); (b) decisions taken from a stale base - a single AddVoter becomes the two-server change {A,B,C}->{A,B,E}, which silently drops a voter, and with a partitioned old voter produces concurrent leaders over the same log, truncation of the entry the stale leader had committed and divergent FSM state (receipts d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740, 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e and e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064); (c) stale membership accounting - a resurrected removed voter or a forgotten added voter makes the leader accept writes that the configuration committed in the log has not acknowledged (receipts 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557, and b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 with ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22). Boundary: a snapshot covering the newest configuration entry, or leaving the flag at its default, removes every one of these observations in the controls, and once the stale configuration is adopted nothing re-reads the log for configurations, so it persists until one of three events repairs it: a snapshot is installed (the configuration comes from the snapshot metadata), a later configuration entry reaches the node through appendEntries and is processed by processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1569-1578, which installs the full membership the leader computed), or the node is restarted without the flag. In the empty-configuration cases the first two repairs need a leader, which is exactly what the empty configuration prevents. A repeat of the simultaneous-restart experiment reproduced the same failure and control values, so the headline progress claim also rests on two scored executions. Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3). Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true). Receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c from the corrected harness scored both comparisons: entry at index 11 truncated after heal (violated, witness index 4) and a_still_leader=true while the old side elected B in term 4 (violated, witness index 3), with the silent change itself at index 2 (change_err nil, committed=true, LogConfiguration on A and E, B at log index 10). The repeat receipt 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e reproduced the same outcome under schedule variation (setup catch-up indices differed: C ended at log index 8 instead of 9): silent change committed at index 11 with entry type LogConfiguration on A and E (index 2), B elected in term 4 while A still led in term 3 (index 3, comparison violated), and the entry truncated after healing (index 4, comparison violated). Receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 (extended harness) scores both comparisons violated with witness index 5: the entry at the created index is truncated after healing, and after a client command returned success and was acknowledged and committed on the {A,B,E} leader (parsed index 3: write_applied=true, applied_a=12, fsm_a_logs=6) the FSM contents differ afterwards (fsm_a_logs=6 versus fsm_b_logs=5), so the client-visible effect survives only on the node whose log lost the entry.  A fourth consequence direction belongs to the client contracts: on the same stale leader, VerifyLeader confirms leadership from the stale quorum while a different majority of the committed configuration elects a leader in a higher term (receipt 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903, witness index 6), so the read-safety protection clients rely on is not effective in that state. Why the competing-majority outcome is attributable to the stale base rather than to the partition: with a correct configuration the same partition geometry cannot commit the change at all, because the change installs its own membership into the commitment and that membership still contains the partitioned voter, so its quorum cannot be reached (a single-server change from {A,B,C} needs two of three including the partitioned member's replacement geometry, and in the four-voter case the new quorum is three of four). The stale base both shrinks the base the change is computed from and replaces a voter, which is why the new member set's quorum can be met by A plus one other node while the partitioned voter stays out - and that is precisely what the D2 receipts show, with the control mode refusing the same write under the committed membership. Mechanism locators for the two steps that turn the stale base into those outcomes: the new configuration is installed into the leader's commitment as soon as the change entry is appended (raft.go 1236-1241), which is what lets the silently created member set be acknowledged by the stale leader plus one other node, and appendEntries clears a conflicting log suffix when terms differ (raft.go 1522-1553), which is what removes the entry the stale leader had committed once the higher-term leader reaches it; the vote freshness checks that keep the removed voter itself from winning are at raft.go 1731-1746 and 1812-1828.

Interpretation counterevidence: The isolated control receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d scores holds with the identical restart and no snapshot (servers_after=1), so the loss is caused by replaying the committed prefix, not by restart, snapshot absence, or the commit-tracking store.; The snapshot run inside the first receipt (index 5) keeps the configuration, so the defect requires the newest configuration entry to be inside the skipped prefix; a snapshot taken after the change masks it.; Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.; The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.; Receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 scores the control comparison holds (index 3: the two live voters re-elect a leader without the flag) and the failing case violated (index 1: after the configured voter stops, no leader among the two live voters although both hold every committed entry, log last index 13 on both), so the loss of electability is tied to the missing configuration rather than to the restart or the shutdown.; The dual-majority path needs a caught-up nonvoter E so the silent change can commit without the partitioned voter B; without such a node the change would need B's acknowledgement and B would then hold the new membership.; Two independent executions of the corrected dual-majority experiment (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c and 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e) produced the same entry index, the same concurrent leadership and the same truncation, so the outcome is reproducible rather than a single-run timing artifact.; In that extended execution the stale leader had already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled (index 4, a_still_leader=false), which is why leader concurrency is reported as an observed window from the two earlier executions rather than as a comparison in the current harness.; Repeat receipt c1dcda29549b48c7a775adfc2e9a4bda reproduced the simultaneous-restart outcome exactly (servers_after [0,0,0], nodes_with_full_config 0, no leader in the observation window; control [3,3,3] with a leader elected at index 3), so the cluster-wide progress loss is reproducible under schedule variation (the staged commit indices differed from the first run: [11 10 11] against [11 11 9]).; Repeat receipt e0ef28c2bc89481aa6b3af478422de7c reproduced all three modes of the original probe with the same values: with RestoreCommittedLogs and no snapshot the node returns with an empty configuration and does not lead again (index 1), while the non-replay mode keeps its configuration and leads (index 3) and the snapshot mode keeps its configuration and leads (index 5).; control re-electing at index 0), so the live-quorum progress loss is reproducible as well.; The revised dual-majority execution (receipt 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903) scored all three comparisons as predicted: the committed entry is truncated after healing (violated, witness 7), the FSMs diverge after an acknowledged write (violated, witness 7, fsm_a_logs 6 against fsm_b_logs 5), and the stale leader confirmed leadership while the old majority led in a higher term (violated, witness 6: verify_ok true, old_leader B in term 4, a_still_leader true).; The repeat of the client-contract revision (receipt 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74) reproduced all three comparison outcomes (truncation violated at witness 7, FSM divergence violated at witness 7, confirmation-while-another-leader violated at witness 6 with verify_ok true, old_leader B in term 4 and A still leading), so that consequence is reproducible.; The repair execution also acts as counterevidence against reading the stale configuration as irrecoverable: a later configuration entry from a correctly configured leader restored the forgotten voter on the restarted node (receipt 6d6abaf163524e64878c6c9810de2461, comparison and witness index 5).; Boundary control: with the same operations but without the commits that push the persisted commit index past the removal entry, the restarted node keeps the committed membership and the removed voter stays removed (receipt 457abd18451d4fd18ed506ae7f5c5391, comparison and witness index 9), so the loss is tied to the entry lying inside the replayed prefix and not to the restart or the removal itself.; The boundary control repeated: receipt 4fe974e4e3cc491984791b8a812c5886 reproduced every comparison of the boundary revision (resurrection violated at index 1, premature commit violated at index 3, flag-off control holding at index 7, and the shallow case holding at index 9 with two servers and the removed voter absent), so the trigger boundary is reproducible and not a schedule artifact.; Counterevidence that limits the impact of the cluster-wide loss rather than the finding: the same stores, restarted once more with the flag disabled, came back fully configured and elected a leader (receipt 81163da076c64417bd48e0f79260d73d, comparison and witness index 2), so the state is operator-recoverable without touching durable data.; Interpretation limitations: All executions are in-process in-memory clusters at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts and a single committed configuration change; joint-consensus or multi-step changes are not exercised.; The finding is specific to RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag disabled the same durable state recovers normally in every receipt.; The configuration-less nodes still act as voters in other respects (they granted the configured voter's election win in receipt 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837, index 0), which is why the cluster survived until that voter stopped; this is read from the receipt and from the membership checks being skipped for an empty configuration (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).; In that probe the partitioned side elects its leader with 3s election timeouts (reloaded to keep the restarted leader from losing the first election), so the interval is seconds; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.; The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).; Leader concurrency on the two sides was observed with A still leading in four executions (receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e, 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903 and 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74) while one revision of the harness observed A already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled, so the window is real but its length is schedule-dependent; control refuses the same write), so the parents' consequence list includes premature commitment under a stale membership.; Two consequences reached by later receipts are no longer pending: the cluster-wide and partial-restart progress losses (receipts 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a and 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837) and the premature-commit-under-a-stale-membership consequence (receipt 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 with its repeat 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557).; A source check of which snapshot the library considers newest found the expected protection: SnapshotStore implementations rank candidates by term then index (file_snapshot.go 535-547 with List at 286), so the newest snapshot is selected; no evidence of a snapshot-selection defect was found, and none is claimed.; The third consequence direction is now established by retained receipt b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691: a restarted leader that forgets an added voter accepted a write held by only two of the four committed voters, while the control refused it.; A check of the captured documentation found no statement about this feature outside the source: RestoreCommittedLogs and CommitTrackingLogStore appear only in config.go, log.go and api.go, and never in README.md, docs/README.md, docs/apply.md, docs/divergence.md, membership.md or CHANGELOG.md (those files do mention snapshots elsewhere, so the search itself is sound). The only normative text is the Config field comment, which requires the commit-tracking store but nothing about snapshots or configuration recovery, so no documented caller duty defeats the premise.; In the original probe and its repeat the two control modes share the comparison event names with the failing mode, so their comparisons are scored unknown; the scored control for the non-replay restart comes from the separate isolated-control experiment (receipt edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d, holds).; Correction of the repair-path statement: an earlier version of the summary said only a snapshot install or an operator restart repairs a stale configuration. A later configuration entry does too, because appendEntries processes new configuration entries and installs the membership encoded in them (raft.go 1569-1578); the three repair paths are now stated explicitly. Boundary that follows: repair needs a correctly configured leader, so it is available where the stale nodes are a minority (the forgotten-voter case) and unavailable where the empty configuration prevents any leader from being elected (the cluster-wide and partial-restart cases).; Process note kept for traceability: receipt 8f0b76d0cd49441c81ecb603f1fcd527 is a build failure of the superseded revision of the partial-restart harness (helpers declared in a sibling file that is not copied for execution); my repeat request had named that superseded experiment instead of its correction b826595f01b844f9b95efe7b29d757dd-experiment. The receipt carries no evidence and is deliberately absent from this interpretation's executions map because a build failure yields no parsed observations; the cited partial-restart observations come only from the corrected revision.; The trigger boundary is now executed in both directions by receipt 457abd18451d4fd18ed506ae7f5c5391: in the shallow case the staged commit index is 5 while the removal entry sits at index 6, so the scan covers it and the restarted node keeps the committed membership (comparison holds at index 9: two servers, removed voter absent, one peer, and the partitioned write refused), whereas the same harness with two extra commits has the removal entry at index 7 with staged commit 7 and resurrects the removed voter (violated at index 1) and accepts the write (violated at index 3; control holds at index 7). The condition 'configuration entry at or below the persisted commit index' in the trigger summary is therefore execution-confirmed rather than reasoned.; Boundary of the empty-configuration case, kept explicit because it limits the consequence: what is lost is membership context and the ability to campaign, not data flow. In the partial-restart receipts (7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837 and its repeat 2963a0b01d97404dbf946e7b87a214f8) the two configuration-less nodes still appended and applied entries up to log index 13 while the correctly configured voter led, and they still granted the votes that let it win, so replication through a configured leader continues; the observable harm is their empty self-view (no campaigns, no peers) and, once the configured voter stops, the cluster-wide loss of electability recorded in those same receipts.; Citation audit: every receipt index cited by the current interpretations was re-read from the retained observations and matches the claim it supports (empty configuration and no leadership at 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1 and its repeat e0ef28c2bc89481aa6b3af478422de7c index 1; silent change, concurrent leader and truncation at 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c indices 2, 3, 4; leader confirmation, confirmation-while-another-leader and truncation plus FSM divergence at 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903 indices 4, 6, 7 and confirmation-while-another-leader again at 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74 index 6; stale membership and the dropped voter at d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 indices 1 and 3; applied client write and FSM divergence at e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 indices 3 and 5; resurrection and premature commit at 226f9762f0b444f69c154b35fe0788f3 indices 1 and 3 and their repeat 7adf927d528b4a74942c03b155aa8557 indices 1 and 3; forgotten voter and understated quorum at b1daa1f4c9444b8d857bc7e0ab761691 indices 1 and 3 and repeat ec2c61af79bd42d7a5fe00657b7aeb22 indices 1 and 3; repair at 6d6abaf163524e64878c6c9810de2461 index 5; boundary at 457abd18451d4fd18ed506ae7f5c5391 indices 1 and 9 and its repeat 4fe974e4e3cc491984791b8a812c5886 indices 1 and 9).; Reachability boundary on the snapshot repair path: although an installed snapshot does carry the configuration (raft.go 1953-1961), a leader sends a snapshot only when the follower lacks entries the leader has already compacted, and a node whose configuration was lost this way has a complete log (the loss comes from skipping entries, not from missing them), so no snapshot is sent to it in these scenarios (with the caveat, found while re-reading the snapshot path, that a leader-side user restore leaves a hole above such a node's next index and does send it one, replication.go 222-224 with raft.go 1097-1199). The snapshot path therefore repairs new or behind nodes, while a stale-but-complete node is repaired only by an operator restart without the flag or by a later configuration entry from a correctly configured leader, as executed.; Operator recovery is now executed (receipt 0440f054115e44f4a0234c7a4ef67150): in the empty-configuration state live bootstrap refuses with 'bootstrap only works on new clusters' and leaves the node empty (violated, index 1), while RecoverCluster on the stopped node restores the supplied configuration and the node leads again within three seconds (holds, index 2). The repair picture is therefore complete and operational: a later configuration entry from a correctly configured leader, a restart with the flag disabled, or RecoverCluster on a stopped node; not live bootstrap, and not an incoming snapshot for a node whose log is already complete.; The operator remediation for the cluster-wide case is now executed (receipt 81163da076c64417bd48e0f79260d73d): the flagged simultaneous restart left every voter empty with no leader (violated, index 1, staged commit indices [11 11 11]), and stopping the same three nodes and restarting them on the same stores with the flag disabled restored the configuration on all three and produced a leader (holds at index 2, nodes_with_full_config 3, leader index 1; control unchanged at index 4). The consequence of the headline progress loss is therefore bounded: it is in-memory and reversible by an ordinary restart, with no durable state discarded and no configuration change needed, but nothing in-protocol can repair it while it lasts.; Precision on what the truncation removes, taken from the same receipts rather than reasoned: in both executions that carry the client write (e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 index 5 and 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903 index 7) the stale leader's log end falls from index 12 to 11 after healing while its applied index stays at 12 and its FSM still holds six commands against the new leader's five. The entry removed is therefore not only the configuration change at index 11 but also the client command the leader had committed and applied at index 12, and the two sides' applied state differs by exactly that command. This is the client-visible form of the safety violation: an acknowledged write is deleted from the log of the node that acknowledged it, while the divergent FSM keeps its effect.; The causal refinement is executed (receipt 656e33fb90f24c58a94928eeeeb938aa): the cluster that had only run with the flag disabled carried a staged commit index of 0 and kept its configuration through the first flagged restart (comparison holds, index 1), then staged 9 through its own writes while the flag was on (index 2) and lost the configuration on the next flagged restart (violated, witness index 3, zero servers and no leader). The trigger is therefore the persisted commit index relative to the newest configuration entry, not the flag by itself, and the first restart after enabling the feature can look harmless.; The latent-trap experiment has been executed twice with identical values (receipts 656e33fb90f24c58a94928eeeeb938aa and 202311f4911e4af5828d49134f37811c), so the causal refinement rests on a reproduced contrast rather than a single run.; Traceability note on one knowledge record, so a reviewer is not misled by its evidence list: two submissions that supplied the repair Fact's sources and executions were accepted but not reflected in the stored entry (revisions 4 and 5 keep four source ids and three receipts). Its statement and conditions are the corrected ones, and the evidence exists in the rest of the record: the in-protocol repair by a later configuration entry is receipt 6d6abaf163524e64878c6c9810de2461 index 5, cited in the parent and in the forgotten-voter interpretation and executed with its own comparisons; the operator paths are receipt 0440f054115e44f4a0234c7a4ef67150 (live bootstrap refusing at index 1, RecoverCluster repairing at index 2) and 81163da076c64417bd48e0f79260d73d (flag-disabled restart restoring all voters at index 2), both cited here; and the source anchors that the entry's list omits are the bootstrap refusal (api.go 260-267), RecoverCluster (api.go 321-448), the snapshot trigger (replication.go 222-224) and the user-restore hole (raft.go 1097-1199), all of which are declared in this submission's sources.; Artifact check: the ten harness files in this draft were hashed against the controller's fixed copies, and each current experiment's harness matches the draft byte for byte (primary probe 9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3, gap probe 8efd0d1e3da9484e926cab983024d9c3, partial-restart correction b826595f01b844f9b95efe7b29d757dd, cluster-wide remediation d2938865782c439380ed920dd69f8d7a, dual-majority verify revision cae69864c3a4406ba6f2c5d594bda44c, resurrect boundary revision dd13767ee8154cd3b8253d6352f679da, understate repair revision 6856b3402bb5458ba40e94f9f7e3ea00, operator recovery 82a49b6bfe414dbab6903379c966b105, isolated control d2cb2558b564427ba5f166e377991a07, latent trap eb30543c698b432c8f570dbfc31951f6). The fixed copies that do not match a current draft file are the superseded revisions of those same lineages (81237e6441414088bfb2079263cc63ec, a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f, cdee42fcadd7460991a44622a9725658, 981f67969ef44bc1b4d8e296cbb610c4, cff2222705354f669ca24cef6629804a, f79f8f8c97204c7d9c76b1a2b8ca07a0, d5ed22414b9d439e9d0fcd0b06849027, dd5cdfe7274a4444b305c5d104f6e5c8), which is the expected state: their receipts remain valid for the comparisons they scored, and the current bytes are the corrected revisions.; Detection, from the fields this investigation already read rather than from a new API: GetConfiguration and Stats report the node's in-memory configuration and its index (api.go 1231-1237 and the GetConfiguration accessor), so the state is found by comparing that configuration with the configuration a peer reports or with the newest configuration entry in the node's own store, not by a threshold on indexes. The two forms observed here are an empty in-memory configuration (the empty case, seen as zero servers and zero peers while the node still holds a complete log) and an in-memory configuration older than the newest configuration entry in that node's log (the stale case, e.g. two servers while peers report three or four). One caution against a false positive: latest_configuration_index being below commit_index is normal, because a configuration entry stays the latest until a later configuration entry appears while ordinary entries continue to commit, so that comparison alone does not indicate this state.; Protection direction, following directly from the traced mechanism rather than from any new claim: the state exists because the configuration scan begins after the replayed committed prefix (api.go 611-613), so scanning configuration entries from the snapshot index onward instead of from max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 would leave the replayed entries applied to the FSM while still rebuilding the configuration from the log; and because the failure is silent, a start-time check that compares the reconstructed configuration with the newest configuration entry the node's own log or snapshot carries (and refuses to serve, or reports, when a voter's configuration is empty or older than that entry) would surface the state where indexes alone cannot, since the log is complete and commit and applied indexes look healthy.; Source-anchor audit of this submission's own grounding, run in the closing pass and reported because it is checkable rather than new evidence: all 24 declared sources were re-read from the captured tree and each one still lands on the code or text it is cited for, including the load-bearing anchors of the finding (the configuration scan and its max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 bound at api.go 601-622, restoreFromCommittedLogs raising lastApplied to the commit-tracking store's index at api.go 723-755, the snapshot-configuration restore at api.go 645-689 and processConfigurationLogEntry at raft.go 1605-1623) and the anchors of the consequences and boundaries (raft.go 1663-1672 and 1780-1784 for the skipped membership checks, raft.go 1204-1241 and 1236-1241 for configuration-change admission and commit-on-append, configuration.go 224-302 for nextConfiguration, raft.go 964-988 for the verifyLeader quorum, raft.go 1953-1961 and 1569-1578 for the two repair-by-installation paths, api.go 260-267 and api.go 321-448 for the bootstrap refusal and RecoverCluster, replication.go 222-224 with raft.go 1097-1199 for the snapshot trigger and the user-restore hole). No anchor was found to be off by a line or attached to a different construct, so no correction followed from the audit; it is recorded here because the whole account rests on these ranges having been read in the captured tree rather than in an editor.; Scoped-negative extension and one added source anchor, both from the closing pass. First, the earlier documentation check is widened from the named markdown files to the whole captured tree: a recursive search for RestoreCommittedLogs and CommitTrackingLogStore over all 91 captured files returns only six Go files (api.go, config.go, inmem_store.go, log.go, raft.go, raft_test.go) and no non-Go surface at all, so the 26 non-Go files - README.md, docs/README.md, docs/apply.md, docs/divergence.md, membership.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CHANGELOG.md, fuzzy/readme.md, the .github templates and workflows, the Makefile and the module files - carry no statement about this feature. The negative is still scoped to the captured tree, not to upstream releases. Second, the source that writes the condition the trigger depends on is now anchored: tryStageCommitIndex (raft.go 1392-1404) stages the commit index into the store only when RestoreCommittedLogs is enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore, and InmemCommitTrackingStore declares that interface (inmem_store.go:12), which is the code-level reason a cluster that never ran with the flag carries a staged value of zero and one that has run with it carries the commit index - the contrast the latent-trap receipts measure. No receipt, comparison or conclusion changed.

The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).; a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1: model declares resolved: Resolved affirmatively by retained receipts 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c, 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e, 1f95cb0a02bc4577a5a9f1ab627fe903 and 108a83830e904d90a9236738033c2c74: the silently created two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} commits on the stale leader A plus the promoted, caught-up nonvoter E while the old voter B is partitioned (witness index 2 in each execution: change_err nil, committed true, the configuration entry present on A and on E, B still one index short); the old majority {B,C} then elects B in a higher term while A still leads its own configuration with E's acknowledgements (witness index 3 or 6: old_leader B in term 4 with a_still_leader true); and after the partition heals A's committed entry is replaced by the new leader's entry (witness index 7, committed_entry_truncated true), leaving the two sides with different logs and different applied state (fsm_a_logs 6 against fsm_b_logs 5). The direct route the earlier answer identified as impossible stays impossible - a voter that never receives the entry is strictly behind and is refused by voters that hold it (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) - which is exactly why the construction needs the entry to commit without one old voter, made possible by the promoted nonvoter and by the new configuration entering the commitment on append (raft.go 1236-1241).; 1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2: model declares resolved: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The earlier receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced the same observations but its comparisons were unscored because of my identity wiring; it is retained as the superseded revision of the same harness.
Hypothesis: No. restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so the configuration scan starts after the committed prefix and never calls processConfigurationLogEntry for the configuration entry that only exists in the log. r.configurations.latest stays empty (or stays at the snapshot configuration), so the node loses its own membership context, cannot start elections, and skips the membership checks when granting votes.
Registered discriminator: Restart the same durable state twice: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and with RestoreCommittedLogs=false. Predict servers_after=0 and no re-election with the feature on, versus servers_after=1 and a successful re-election with it off. A third run takes a snapshot before restart to show that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss (servers_after=1), separating the scanning bound from generic restart damage.

Fixed experiment `9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-experiment` v1: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: In-process single-voter Cluster: bootstrap a configuration entry, become leader, apply five commands, then restart the node on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore with a fresh transport. Three cases: restore_committed_logs on with no snapshot; off with no snapshot; on with a snapshot taken before the restart. Observations are the node's configuration size (GetConfiguration), whether it reaches Leader again, applied/commit indices, and staged commit index at restart.
History / supplied conditions: Fresh in-memory transport, InmemCommitTrackingStore log store, InmemStore stable store, InmemSnapshotStore; BootstrapCluster writes the single-voter configuration at index 1/term 1; first NewRaft elects the node as leader; five Apply commands are committed; optional user snapshot; Shutdown; second NewRaft on the same stores with a new transport sharing the same address. The harness never fabricates log entries or configuration state: all durable state comes from real bootstrap, real elections, real commits and a real snapshot.
Assumptions: RestoreCommittedLogs is a documented public Config field (config.go 243-254) that is enabled by the application; the probe only supplies that documented configuration.; The existing test TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs always snapshots before restarting (raft_test.go 1183-1280), so the configuration-in-log path is not covered by it.; No snapshot is taken in the no-snapshot cases (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 10m), which is normal operation for clusters below the snapshot threshold.
Excluded scope: Multi-node clusters and network partitions: the probe is a single-voter cluster, so the observed election abort is a progress loss and the vote-check consequence is source-read, not executed here.
Declared requirement / prediction: No fixed requirement; observations remain available for sourced interpretation.

Fixed experiment `8efd0d1e3da9484e926cab983024d9c3-experiment` v1: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/8efd0d1e3da9484e926cab983024d9c3-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: Two-voter in-memory cluster {A,B}: A is bootstrapped with both voters and becomes leader, commands are committed, A takes a snapshot (configuration {A,B} at index 1), then AddVoter C commits a configuration entry at index 8 while A and B are the only running servers. Four further commands push the persisted commit index past index 8. A is shut down and restarted on the same stores with a fresh transport (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false). Observed: the restarted node's configuration membership versus the still-running peer's view and the newest configuration entry in its own log; then, while the restarted node is stably leader, one further AddVoter E and the resulting cluster configuration on both nodes.
History / supplied conditions: Real bootstrap of both voters on A, real election, real applies, real user snapshot on A, real AddVoter C through the cluster, real shutdown and restart of A on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore. Fixed experiment `a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-experiment` v1: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: Three-voter in-memory cluster {A,B,C} bootstrapped on A, converged, ten commands committed, no snapshot. Only voters A and B are restarted (case restore_on with RestoreCommittedLogs=true, control restore_off with it false) while C keeps running; the restarted voters' fresh transports are wired to each other and to C's live transport in both directions. The probe first observes which node leads (C, the only one still holding the configuration, is expected to win with votes from the configuration-less restarted voters), then stops that configured voter and observes whether the two remaining live voters - a quorum of three, each holding every committed entry (log last index 13 on both) - can elect a leader within six seconds at 50ms timeouts.
History / supplied conditions: Real bootstrap and replication to all three voters, real election, real applies, graceful shutdown of A and B only, restart of A and B on the same stores with fresh transports rewired to the live peer, real graceful shutdown of the remaining configured voter. All configuration and log state comes from those operations; the control repeats the identical procedure with RestoreCommittedLogs=false.
Assumptions: Restarting two voters while one keeps running is the ordinary rolling/cold restart an operator may perform; all three stores already contain the bootstrapped configuration entry and every committed entry.; The decision to stop the configured voter afterwards is a normal availability event (the node is gracefully shut down), not a fault injection: two of three voters remain alive and up to date.; A quorum of two live voters with complete logs is entitled to elect a leader in this cluster, which is exactly what the control case measures.
Excluded scope: No partitions, no disk faults, no message loss, no injected delays.; The election fan-out to the stopped node is not traced; the observation is the absence of any leader among the live voters.
Declared requirement / prediction: No fixed requirement; observations remain available for sourced interpretation.

Fixed experiment `cdee42fcadd7460991a44622a9725658-experiment` v1: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/cdee42fcadd7460991a44622a9725658-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B are bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter (config {A,B,C} plus nonvoter E), commits four commands. A is shut down and restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its in-memory configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry; the other three nodes get longer timeouts so the restarted leader wins back leadership. B is then partitioned from A (C is already absent from A's stale configuration, so A replicates to nobody but E), and A issues one AddVoter E. Observations: whether that change commits and with whose acknowledgement, each side's configuration and log tail, who leads each side and in which term, and the content of A's log at the created entry index before and after the partition is healed.
History / supplied conditions: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddNonvoter catch-up, real AddVoter, real commits, graceful shutdown and restart of the leader on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real transport partition and real healing. The log, snapshot metadata and configurations all come from those operations; the harness never fabricates entries or configuration state.
Assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, which is what lets the silently-created {A,B,E} configuration commit with A and E alone once B is partitioned; this is ordinary use of AddNonvoter followed by AddVoter.; Restarting the leader with RestoreCommittedLogs=true is the documented configuration already established by the earlier receipts; nothing else about the cluster changes.; The partition is applied by disconnecting the in-memory transports in both directions, which is a real partition for all Raft traffic (AppendEntries, heartbeats, votes).; Both sides keep following the protocol: A leads the {A,B,E} configuration with E's acknowledgements, and B and C campaign under their own {A,B,C} configuration after their election timeout.
Excluded scope: No control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter adds a single server and the two-server change cannot arise; that is a source-level statement (nextConfiguration over the current configuration) rather than an execution.; No disk faults or message loss; the only partition is the one applied explicitly.
Declared requirement / prediction: No fixed requirement; observations remain available for sourced interpretation.

Can running nodes then hold disjoint majorities (old {A,B,C} majority without E versus new {A,B,E} majority without C) and elect two leaders in different terms for the same log?; Can the silently-created two-server change ({A,B,C} -> {A,B,E}, committed with A plus a promoted caught-up nonvoter E while B is partitioned) let the old majority {B,C} elect a leader in a higher term that then truncates A's committed entry X when the partition heals, and can the two sides therefore hold leaders of different terms over the same log?

Fixed experiment `f79f8f8c97204c7d9c76b1a2b8ca07a0-experiment` v3: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/f79f8f8c97204c7d9c76b1a2b8ca07a0-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: Four in-process nodes at protocol version 3 with 300ms heartbeat/election/lease: A and B bootstrapped as voters {A,B}; A snapshots, adds E as a caught-up nonvoter, adds C as a voter, commits four commands. A is restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs=true so its configuration comes from the snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds {A,B,C}; B is partitioned; A issues AddVoter E, which the stale base turns into the two-server change {A,B,E} and which commits on A plus E. The probe then issues one client command on A (committed with A and E) and finally heals the partition, observing the entry at the created index and the FSM contents of A and of the old-majority leader.
History / supplied conditions: Real bootstrap, real snapshot, real AddNonvoter catch-up, real AddVoter, real commits, graceful shutdown and restart of the leader on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances, real client Apply, real transport partition and real healing. Nothing is fabricated.
Assumptions: E is a caught-up nonvoter before the change, so {A,B,E} commits with A and E alone once B is partitioned.; The client command is an ordinary Apply on the leader that has a quorum of the configuration recorded in its own log ({A,B,E}: A and E).; MockFSM records one entry per LogCommand applied, so its length is the number of committed commands that node's FSM has consumed.; Both sides keep running the protocol; the partition is applied by disconnecting in-memory transports in both directions.
Excluded scope: No control variant: with the flag disabled the configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create the disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration).; Leader concurrency is not asserted as a comparison here because its window depends on when the higher-term vote requests reach the stale leader.

It also drops the earlier 'at most one leader' comparison because a construction-time run of this revision observed A stepping down before the old side's leader was sampled (vote requests in the higher term reach A from the connected side), so the leader-concurrency window is schedule-dependent and is retained as an observation from the two scored executions rather than as a comparison in this harness.; actual changes: harness, source_ids, scope, prefix, comparisons

Scope: Same four-node scenario as the executed revision (A/B bootstrapped, A snapshots, E added as a caught-up nonvoter, C added as a voter, A restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs so its configuration is the stale {A,B}, B partitioned, AddVoter E committing the two-server change {A,B,E} on A plus E, one client command applied on A), with one addition: while A still leads on the stale membership, the probe calls VerifyLeader on A and records the result, then observes whether the old majority {B,C} elects a leader in a higher term, and emits both together.

Assumptions: VerifyLeader is the documented protection clients use to avoid returning stale data from a peer that has lost leadership.; The stale leader's confirmation uses the acknowledgements available to it under its in-memory configuration {A,B,E}, which is exactly the configuration its own log does not contain.; The old majority's election is decided independently of the stale leader because B is partitioned from A.

Fixed experiment `d2938865782c439380ed920dd69f8d7a-experiment` v2: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/d2938865782c439380ed920dd69f8d7a-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: Three-voter in-process cluster at protocol version 3 with 50ms heartbeat/election timeouts: bootstrap on A, replication to B and C, ten commits, no snapshot, simultaneous graceful shutdown of all three, restart with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled (failing mode) or disabled (control). In the failing mode the probe then stops the three nodes again and restarts them with the flag disabled on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances and fresh transports, recording each node's configuration and whether a leader appears within eight seconds.
History / supplied conditions: Real bootstrap, real replication, real commits, real graceful shutdowns and restarts on the same stores with fresh transports; the recovery phase uses the same stores and the same configuration with the flag disabled, and no other change.
Assumptions: The second restart differs from the first only in the flag, so any change in the outcome is attributable to the restart path rather than to the stores, which are the same instances.; The operator restart is the natural remediation an operator would attempt after noticing the empty configurations, and it does not require discarding the durable state.
Excluded scope: No RecoverCluster in this harness: the operator paths on a stopped node are covered by the dedicated single-voter harness and its receipt.; The control mode keeps its original two phases, so its earlier comparisons retain their meaning.

Fixed experiment `eb30543c698b432c8f570dbfc31951f6-experiment` v1: [saved basis](fixed-experiments/eb30543c698b432c8f570dbfc31951f6-experiment/basis.json).
Scope: Single-voter in-process cluster at protocol version 3 with 50ms timeouts whose log store is a CommitTrackingLogStore. The node runs and commits five commands with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled, so nothing is staged; it is then restarted with the flag enabled and the staged value still zero, commits two further commands so the flag-on path stages a commit index, and is restarted once more with the flag still enabled. Every phase records the staged commit index, the configuration size and whether a leader appears.
History / supplied conditions: Real bootstrap, real election, real commits with the flag disabled, graceful shutdown, restart with the flag enabled, real commits while enabled, graceful shutdown, restart again with the flag enabled, all on the same InmemCommitTrackingStore/InmemStore/InmemSnapshotStore instances. Nothing is fabricated.
Assumptions: tryStageCommitIndex returns early when RestoreCommittedLogs is disabled, so a cluster that has only ever run with the flag off has no staged commit index even though its log holds committed entries; the observation records the staged value rather than assuming it.; The two restarts differ only in whether the store has a staged commit index at that moment, so any difference in the outcome is attributable to that value rather than to the flag alone.
Excluded scope: No multi-voter cluster and no configuration change: the question is which condition triggers the loss, not what the loss causes.
Declared requirement / prediction: No fixed requirement; observations remain available for sourced interpretation.

Interpretation history:


Historical interpretation `9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-interpretation-0` · source explanation; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); nothing waives configuration recovery. The code nevertheless bounds the configuration scan by max(lastSnapshot, lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613) while restoreFromCommittedLogs has already raised lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755). processConfigurationLogEntry is the only path that turns a log entry into r.configurations (raft.go 1605-1623), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are dropped whenever a snapshot does not carry them (snapshot path: api.go 645-689). Consequence: after a plain restart of a bootstrapped node with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and no snapshot, r.configurations.latest is empty, so runFollower refuses to campaign ('no known peers', raft.go 230-234) and both requestVote and requestPreVote skip their membership checks because they are gated on a non-empty Servers list (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784). The rule that decides the decision is therefore evaluated against an empty configuration rather than the replicated one.

Sources: [newraft_scan](state.json), [restore_committed](state.json), [newraft_doc](state.json), [cfg_doc](state.json), [snapshot_config](state.json), [process_config_entry](state.json), [follower_abort](state.json), [vote_config_checks](state.json), [prevote_config_checks](state.json); execution evidence: No execution receipt explicitly cited by this interpretation.
Interpretation counterevidence: The existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs (raft_test.go 1183-1280) passes: it always snapshots before restarting, so its configuration comes from snapshot metadata rather than from the log, and the same probe shows that a snapshot-carried configuration masks the loss.; The loss is not caused by the commit-tracking store or by replaying logs to the FSM per se: the control restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores and log contents keeps the configuration and wins the election again.
Interpretation limitations: The executed probe is a single-voter in-memory cluster; the multi-node consequences (a node that grants votes to servers it cannot be shown to contain, or a node whose quorum size is computed from a stale configuration) are read from source, not executed.; The persisted commit index used at restart is what the store reported (6 while the log ended at 7); the drop of the configuration entry does not depend on that lag, but the exact boundary of what is skipped does.; Whether upstream intends applications to always snapshot before enabling this option is not stated anywhere in the captured sources; the Config documentation mentions no such requirement.

Historical interpretation `8efd0d1e3da9484e926cab983024d9c3-interpretation-0` · declared predicate does not hold; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): Observed in the retained execution: after restart with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot, the node's configuration is empty (event index 1: mode=restore_on_no_snapshot, servers_before=1, servers_after=0, config_preserved=false, snapshot_count=0, staged_commit=6, log_last_index=7) and it never campaigns again (became_leader=false after a 3s opportunity, with the node logging 'no known peers, aborting election'), while the two controls keep the configuration and re-elect (index 3 restore_off_no_snapshot: servers_after=1, became_leader=true; index 5 restore_on_with_snapshot: servers_after=1, snapshot_count=1, became_leader=true). Source account of the mechanism: NewRaft documents that existing state such as logs and peers is restored (api.go 504-507) and RestoreCommittedLogs is documented only as replaying committed logs before startup (config.go 243-254); restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755) and the configuration scan then starts at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never turned into r.configurations by their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty, runFollower refuses to start an election (raft.go 230-234) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784).

Sources: [newraft_scan](state.json), [restore_committed](state.json), [newraft_doc](state.json), [cfg_doc](state.json), [snapshot_config](state.json), [process_config_entry](state.json), [follower_abort](state.json), [vote_config_checks](state.json), [prevote_config_checks](state.json); execution evidence: [430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc](logs/430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc/check.json) ([observations](logs/430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc/observations.json), event indices [1]).
Interpretation counterevidence: The repository's own TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs (raft_test.go 1183-1280) passes because it always snapshots before restarting; the executed snapshot control (index 5) shows the same masking, so the failing case is specifically a configuration that lives only in the skipped committed log prefix.; Restarting identical durable state with RestoreCommittedLogs=false keeps servers_after=1 and re-elects (index 3), so neither the commit-tracking store nor replaying logs to the FSM is the cause.; The node still has all committed entries on disk (log_last_index=7 > commit_index=6), so this is a lost configuration context, not lost data; the entry itself is present and would be re-read only if a snapshot were installed.
Interpretation limitations: Executed scope is a single-voter in-memory cluster (protocol version 3, heartbeat/election 50ms); the multi-node consequences (votes granted to servers the node cannot show it contains, quorum size and configuration changes computed from a stale base) are read from source and are the subject of the registered gap.; The restart uses the commit index the store reported (6, log end 7); the boundary of the skipped prefix depends on that value, but the omission of the configuration entry does not.; Nothing in the captured sources requires an application to snapshot before enabling RestoreCommittedLogs, so the failing condition is reachable through the documented configuration alone.

Historical interpretation `8efd0d1e3da9484e926cab983024d9c3-interpretation-1` · source explanation; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): Registered gap answered by source trace plus a construction-time run of this probe. Source: a restarted node adopts the snapshot's configuration whenever the newest configuration entry lies inside the skipped committed prefix (api.go 611-613 with 723-755, snapshot path api.go 645-689), and appendConfigurationEntry then computes the next configuration from that stale r.configurations.latest (raft.go 1204-1241) once configurationChangeChIfStable admits the change because latest and committed indexes look equal (raft.go 654-664); nextConfiguration derives the new membership from that same base (configuration.go 328-406). Observed at construction time (native run, pending retained receipt): with RestoreCommittedLogs=true the restarted node reports 2 servers while its peer still reports 3 and its own log's newest configuration entry (index 8) is below the persisted commit index (11); the next AddVoter then committed successfully (err=nil) with the cluster converging on 3 servers without C, so voter C was legitimately added and then silently removed without any request removing it. The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 servers and the later change produced 4 members including C.

Sources: [newraft_scan](state.json), [restore_committed](state.json), [snapshot_config](state.json), [append_config_entry](state.json), [next_configuration](state.json), [cfg_change_gate](state.json); execution evidence: No execution receipt explicitly cited by this interpretation.
Interpretation counterevidence: The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false on identical stores preserved all three members and added E without dropping C, so the stale base is specific to the skipped committed prefix rather than to config changes in general.
Interpretation limitations: This is a construction-time native reproduction; the formal receipt for this harness is requested in this update and the claim is retained as explained/unresolved-for-receipt until it exists.; C never runs, so the probe cannot show whether C would itself notice or resist its removal; that is about C's own state, not about the decision the restarted node made.; The removal happens through a successful public AddVoter, so the consequence is reachable through the ordinary configuration API, but only while the restarted node is leader and its stale latest/committed indexes look equal.
Gap responses: 9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0: gap remains open: Yes for both parts, subject to the retained receipt for this probe: the stale configuration is adopted when the snapshot predates the committed configuration entry, and it does justify a different decision - a configuration change based on the stale membership drops voter C for the whole cluster (observed change_err=nil, both nodes ending with 3 members and contains_c=false), instead of the intended 4-member configuration. Source dependency chain recorded in the rationale; construction-time run reproduced all three predictions, retained execution pending.

Historical interpretation `81237e6441414088bfb2079263cc63ec-interpretation-0` · declared predicate does not hold; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664).

Historical interpretation `81237e6441414088bfb2079263cc63ec-interpretation-1` · source explanation; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): Registered gap answered by source trace plus a construction-time run of this probe. Source: a restarted node adopts the snapshot's configuration whenever the newest configuration entry lies inside the skipped committed prefix (api.go 611-613 with 723-755, snapshot path api.go 645-689), and appendConfigurationEntry then computes the next configuration from that stale r.configurations.latest (raft.go 1204-1241) once configurationChangeChIfStable admits the change because latest and committed indexes look equal (raft.go 654-664); nextConfiguration derives the new membership from that same base (configuration.go 328-406). Observed at construction time (native run, pending retained receipt): with RestoreCommittedLogs=true the restarted node reports 2 servers while its peer still reports 3 and its own log's newest configuration entry (index 8) is below the persisted commit index (11); the next AddVoter then committed successfully (err=nil) with the cluster converging on 3 servers without C, so voter C was legitimately added and then silently removed without any request removing it. The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 servers and the later change produced 4 members including C.

Gap responses: 9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-gap-0: model declares resolved: Resolved by retained receipt d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740: the restarted node adopts the snapshot-carried configuration when the newest configuration entry lies inside the replayed committed prefix (comparison 0 violated, witness index 1: servers_after=2 while the peer reports 3 and the newest configuration entry index 8 is below the staged commit index 11), and that stale base changes a real decision (comparison 2 violated, witness index 3: AddVoter E returned no error and both nodes ended with 3 members and contains_c_final=false, so voter C was silently removed). The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).; a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1: gap remains open: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.

Historical interpretation `1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-interpretation-1` · source explanation; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): Registered gap answered by source trace plus a construction-time run of this probe. Source: a restarted node adopts the snapshot's configuration whenever the newest configuration entry lies inside the skipped committed prefix (api.go 611-613 with 723-755, snapshot path api.go 645-689), and appendConfigurationEntry then computes the next configuration from that stale r.configurations.latest (raft.go 1204-1241) once configurationChangeChIfStable admits the change because latest and committed indexes look equal (raft.go 654-664); nextConfiguration derives the new membership from that same base (configuration.go 328-406). Observed at construction time (native run, pending retained receipt): with RestoreCommittedLogs=true the restarted node reports 2 servers while its peer still reports 3 and its own log's newest configuration entry (index 8) is below the persisted commit index (11); the next AddVoter then committed successfully (err=nil) with the cluster converging on 3 servers without C, so voter C was legitimately added and then silently removed without any request removing it. The control case with RestoreCommittedLogs=false kept 3 servers and the later change produced 4 members including C.

Voter C never runs in the two-voter probe, so nothing in the receipts shows C resisting or noticing its removal; the claim is about the configuration the running nodes decide with.; The cluster-wide receipt 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a scores the control comparison holds (index 3, nodes_with_full_config=3) and the failing case violated (index 1, nodes_with_full_config=0), so the empty configuration after a simultaneous restart is specific to the replayed committed prefix.; the ordering it demonstrates does not depend on those particular values.; The dual-majority probe has no control variant: with the flag disabled the leader's configuration is current, so the same AddVoter is a single-server change and cannot create disjoint majorities (nextConfiguration over the current configuration, configuration.go 224-302).; Leader concurrency on the two sides was observed in the two scored executions (A still leader in term 3 while B led term 4) but a later construction-time run of the extended harness observed A already stepped down when the old side's leader was sampled, so that window is schedule-dependent; the reproducible consequences are the truncation of the committed entry and the resulting FSM divergence.; The resurrected-voter decision consequence (a write accepted on the leader and the resurrected voter while the committed configuration requires B) is claimed from a construction-time run of the child investigation's harness plus source, with its retained receipt requested in this update.

The same receipt's control mode kept 3 members and ended with 4 including C (observed at parsed index 5; that comparison was scored unknown because both modes shared a result event name, which the dedicated control experiment has now replaced with a scored holds).; a8b8d696ac934beda1434a93b5d7758f-gap-1: gap remains open: Partly answered by source and receipt trace, not yet executed. The obvious route cannot work: a voter that never receives the silently-created {A,B,E} entry is strictly behind in the log, and the log up-to-date check in requestVote/requestPreVote (raft.go 1731-1746, 1812-1828) makes any voter that holds the entry refuse to vote for it, so the removed voter C cannot win alone or with a lagging peer. A disjoint-majority election therefore needs a majority of the OLD configuration whose members all lack the entry, which means the entry must commit without one of the old voters acking it. That is reachable because appendConfigurationEntry installs the new configuration into the commitment immediately on append (raft.go 1238-1240), so {A,B,E} commits with A plus a promoted, already-caught-up nonvoter E, without B. The remaining question is whether the partitioned old voter B can then be elected by the old majority {B,C} in a higher term and truncate A's committed entry X when the partition heals (appendEntries clears the conflicting suffix, raft.go 1541-1552), which would lose a committed entry. Requirements identified: a stale-config leader A that keeps leadership long enough, a caught-up nonvoter E (so the change commits without B), B partitioned for the change, and healing afterwards so the higher-term leader's appendEntries reaches A. The next experiment is designed to that discriminator.; 1ed9540f22fe4fa9bef3b3bda88e22e8-gap-2: model declares resolved: Resolved by retained receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c (scored): the silent two-server change {A,B,C} -> {A,B,E} committed on A plus the promoted caught-up nonvoter E (parsed index 2: change_err nil, x_index 11, committed=true, entry type LogConfiguration on A and on E, A commit index 11, B still at log index 10); the old majority {B,C} elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, comparison violated with witness 3), i.e. two concurrent leaders with disjoint support over the same log; and after healing, A's entry at index 11 became a LogNoop of term 4 (parsed index 4, comparison violated with witness 4), so the entry committed under the configuration recorded in the logs was truncated on the node that had committed it. The earlier receipt 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8 reproduced the same observations but its comparisons were unscored because of my identity wiring; it is retained as the superseded revision of the same harness.

Historical interpretation `1a8ca5d0b10a4e248b1d2d93c8656a9e-interpretation-0` · declared predicate does not hold; model defect claim: defect asserted (subject to independent verification): Three independent receipts, all retained. (1) 430d7ba602ed4666bdfe63a96c71e2fc index 1: with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and no snapshot the restarting node returns with an empty configuration (servers_after=0 against servers_before=1), never campaigns again in a 3s opportunity, and logs 'no known peers, aborting election'; both the non-replay run (index 3) and the snapshot run (index 5) keep the configuration and re-elect. (2) d2d1cb0951b74a2984ec525710e4c740 index 1: with a snapshot carrying {A,B}@1 and a committed AddVoter C at index 8 with staged commit 11, the restarted node reports 2 servers while its continuously running peer reports 3 and its own log still holds the newest configuration entry; index 3: a later AddVoter E then returns no error and both nodes converge on 3 members without C (contains_c_final=false), i.e. a legitimately added voter is silently removed from the cluster by a change computed from the stale base. (3) edfd3c204c654542a8bdb4263f290d4d index 1: the isolated control with RestoreCommittedLogs=false scores holds (servers_after=1 against the same bootstrapped voter), so the replayed committed prefix, not restart itself, is the cause. (4) 4f4a771f03b649c2a5703b0ff279ff3a index 1: restarting all three voters at once with the flag leaves servers_after=[0,0,0] and nodes_with_full_config=0 with no leader in a six-second opportunity, while the same procedure without the flag scores holds at index 3 (nodes_with_full_config=3, leader elected) - a cluster-wide progress loss, not a single node's lost context. (5) 7afe8c0403874dbeb0a917a3ee9ed837: with only two of three voters restarted, the untouched configured voter leads with the configuration-less nodes' votes (index 0, servers_after=[0,0,3]); once that voter stops, the two remaining live, fully up-to-date voters cannot elect a leader in six seconds at 50ms timeouts (index 1, log last index 13 on both), while the control without the flag re-elects immediately (index 3). Source chain: restoreFromCommittedLogs raises lastApplied to the persisted commit index (api.go 723-755); the configuration scan then begins at max(lastSnapshot,lastApplied)+1 (api.go 611-613), so configuration entries inside the committed prefix are never fed to their only producer processConfigurationLogEntry (raft.go 1605-1623) unless a snapshot carries them (api.go 645-689). With Servers empty the follower refuses to campaign (raft.go 230-234 on every heartbeat timeout, raft.go 214-251) and both vote handlers skip their membership checks (raft.go 1663-1672, 1780-1784); with Servers stale, appendConfigurationEntry derives the next membership from that stale base (raft.go 1204-1241, configuration.go 224-302) once the admission gate sees latest==committed (raft.go 654-664). (6) 79d93a5aaad448888cc04214be8f2ad8: with A's configuration coming from a snapshot ({A,B}) while its log holds the newer {A,B,C} entry, AddVoter E returned no error and the silently created two-server change committed at index 11 with A's commit index at 11 and E holding the same LogConfiguration entry (parsed index 2), while B stayed at log index 10 with the old membership; the old majority {B,C} then elected B in term 4 while A was still leader in term 3 (parsed index 3, a_still_leader=true), and after the partition healed A's entry 11 was a LogNoop of term 4 rather than the committed configuration entry (parsed index 4, committed_entry_truncated=true). Receipt 6f9feceeefb245c288a7fd1f4497b83c from the corrected harness scored both comparisons: entry at index 11 truncated after heal (violated, witness index 4) and a_still_leader=true while the old side elected B in term 4 (violated, witness index 3), with the silent change itself at index 2 (change_err nil, committed=true, LogConfiguration on A and E, B at log index 10). The repeat receipt 11dea1fdcb6d4f089a373fe6c1d3a36e reproduced the same outcome under schedule variation (setup catch-up indices differed: C ended at log index 8 instead of 9): silent change committed at index 11 with entry type LogConfiguration on A and E (index 2), B elected in term 4 while A still led in term 3 (index 3, comparison violated), and the entry truncated after healing (index 4, comparison violated). Receipt e5ad9e5149fa4255b61e7826bf6b8064 (extended harness) scores both comparisons violated with witness index 5: the entry at the created index is truncated after healing, and after a client command returned success and was acknowledged and committed on the {A,B,E} leader (parsed index 3: write_applied=true, applied_a=12, fsm_a_logs=6) the FSM contents differ afterwards (fsm_a_logs=6 versus fsm_b_logs=5), so the client-visible effect survives only on the node whose log lost the entry.
